items.stem: Which statement about the greatest common factor (GCF) of $8x^{3}+4x^{2}$ is true?
items.hint: The GCF is the largest number together with the largest power of $x$ that divides BOTH terms exactly.
worked: Coefficients: the largest number dividing both $8$ and $4$ is $4$.
Variables: $8x^{3}$ carries three factors of $x$ and $4x^{2}$ carries two, so the most they share is $x^{2}$. The GCF is $4x^{2}$.
Divide each term by it: $\dfrac{8x^{3}}{4x^{2}}=2x$ and $\dfrac{4x^{2}}{4x^{2}}=1$. A term that divides out exactly leaves a $1$, not nothing.

options.text: The GCF is $4x^{2}$ and the factored form is $4x^{2}(2x)$.
The GCF is $4x$ and the factored form is $4x(2x^{2}+x)$.
The GCF is $4x^{2}$ and the factored form is $4x^{2}(2x+1)$.
The GCF is $4x^{2}$ and the factored form is $4x^{2}(2x^{-1}+1)$.

items.stem: A student factors $-15x^{3}+10x^{2}-5x$ by pulling out $-5x$ and writes $-5x(3x^{2}+2x-1)$. Which of the four expressions below is the correct factorization?
items.hint: Multiply each candidate back out and compare all three signs against the original expression.
worked: Divide every term by the whole GCF $-5x$, negative sign included, not just by $5x$.
Check: $-5x\cdot 3x^{2}=-15x^{3}$, $-5x\cdot(-2x)=10x^{2}$, $-5x\cdot 1=-5x$. The student applied the negative to the first term only.

items.hint: The shared power of $x$ is the SMALLEST one that appears in the expression, and every term has to leave a factor behind.
worked: The largest number dividing $9$, $15$ and $3$ is $3$, and the smallest power of $x$ present is $x^{2}$, so the GCF is $3x^{2}$.
Divide, subtracting exponents top minus bottom: $\dfrac{9x^{6}}{3x^{2}}=3x^{4}$ and $\dfrac{-15x^{4}}{3x^{2}}=-5x^{2}$.
The last term divides out exactly: $\dfrac{3x^{2}}{3x^{2}}=1$.
So $9x^{6}-15x^{4}+3x^{2}=3x^{2}(3x^{4}-5x^{2}+1)$, and $3x^{4}-5x^{2}+1$ has no further factors with integer coefficients.
